pages.text: Tiers 1-4 are single blocks. $(l)Tier 1-2$() print items only; structure printing starts at $(l)Tier 3$() (3×3 footprint) and grows to 5×5 at $(l)Tier 4$().$(br2)Power is Redstone Flux from any side. Losing power $(l)pauses$() a job: progress is never lost, and the print resumes when power returns.
The Tier 1 printer: a piston, a little redstone, and an iron shell. Your first machine.

pages.title: Higher Tiers
pages.text: Higher tiers print $(l)faster$(), cost $(l)less$() per block, and take $(l)more upgrades$() (up to 8 slots). They also unlock higher material tiers.$(br2)Tiers 5-8 are multiblock $(item)Fabricators$(); see Multiblocks.

pages.title: Matter Calculator
pages.text: With a disc loaded the GUI shows the whole bill: total FU and time, and the gauge tooltip breaks it down per tier against what is on hand.$(br2)If a tier cannot be covered the line turns red and names it, so you fix the spools $(l)before$() committing filament.$(br2)$(l)Cancel$() is always safe: restarting $(l)repairs$(), and placed blocks re-cover at zero cost.

pages.title: Remote Terminal
pages.text: Sneak-click a printer with the $(item)Remote Terminal$() to pair, then place the terminal anywhere to open that printer's GUI from across the base.
